title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Despite having lost the source of his religious and political power, Sulyvahn, still wearing his torn robes from the battle, remained in the city's cathedral. The Pontiff set about bringing his knights back to life through necromancy, and had them patrol lower Irithyll as frigid spirits. In addition, his beasts regained control over access to the city and cornered Archdeacon McDonnell, who was leading Aldrich's legion, into the Water Reserve, implying his resolve to bring the city back under his control while Aldrich was still busy digesting Gwyndolin.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: With Pontiff Sulyvahn's rise to power in Irithyll, as well as his complete domination of the Way of White faith within the city, Aldrich's depraved habit became likely to draw unwanted attention to the Pontiff's new "holy" regime. In response, Pontiff Sulyvahn seems to have exiled Aldrich to the Cathedral of the Deep, which specialized in rituals of purification from "stagnant darkness", in hopes that the sacred and serene waters of the Cathedral would contain Aldrich's dark habit. The Pontiff also gave one of his small dolls to Aldrich, in the event that he recovered to a point where he could return home.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: no intention of relinquishing the source of his control over the city and the Way of White so easily. From the ensuing battle Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and defeating the Pontiff, who was forced to clear the way for the ruined cathedral of Anor Londo, leaving the old god Gwyndolin to be devoured by Aldrich.

title: Pontiff Knight
snippet: When Pontiff Sulyvahn plotted to control Irithyll, he corrupted their leaders thanks to the unquenchable Profaned Flame that he found in the ruins of the Profaned Capital. After turning the captains of the army of Irithyll into sorcerers in his service, Sulyvahn also influenced the knights they led, gifting them golden crowns as they helped him seize power. After he took power, the knights would serve as Sulyvahn's watchful eyes and punitive blades. When Aldrich and his Deacons attacked Irithyll, the Pontiff Knights were all slain, and now they are frigid spirits brought back to life by the Pontiff's necromancy. Their swords are now gnawed by the insects of the deep spawned by the Evangelists, and the knights continuously spit dark souls as their bodies were hit and filled by the sorceries of the deacons.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
With Pontiff Sulyvahn relinquishing Gwyndolin, the Saint of the Deep was triumphant, taking up residence in the old Cathedral and beginning to feast on the old god. He would fall into a deep slumber in the process of consuming Gwyndolin, during which he would dream and perceive the form of a young, pale girl in hiding. The Aldrich Faithful guarded the old Cathedral to ward off any intrusion on Aldrich's slumber, with the ancient Silver Knights unwittingly aiding the consumption of their former master.

When the Ashen One seeking the Lords of Cinder arrives at Irithyll to slay Aldrich in their quest, he awakens to defend himself, puppeteering Gwyndolin's magic and body, as well as using a miracle developed from his dreams.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: He gathered an army of deacons, who cast off their red robes and crowns—symbolic of their clerical duties— for new dark-blue ones and swore fealty as Aldrich Faithful, their venerance of the Deep finally codified under Aldrich's banner. He then marched on Irithyll, home to the old gods of Anor Londo and the residence of Chief Deity Gwyndolin. Likely forcing his way through the city's magical barrier, he would confront the forces of Pontiff Sulyvahn, who had no intention of relinquishing his power and authority over the city. From the battle that ensued, Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and forcing him into capitulation. Seemingly, the two eventually struck a deal: the Pontiff would maintain some control over lower Irithyll; in exchange, Aldrich would be granted access to Gwyndolin, who was imprisoned by the Pontiff within the old Cathedral of Anor Londo.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet: In the times of the kingdom of Lothric, things have changed. The beautiful city that once had a glowing sunlight is now cold and dark; the cathedral where the Chosen Undead once fought Ornstein and Smough is now corrupted by the Deep and the home to Gwyndolin, who took his father's title of King of the Gods but fell ill; and the chamber that once held Gwynevere now has nothing but the Sun Princess Ring. A denizen that came from the Painted World, Sulyvahn, infiltrated the city of Irithyll and Gwyndolin's Covenant and later proclaimed himself Pontiff. When Gwyndolin fell ill and became incapable of leading the city and the Covenant, he was forced to retire in the cathedral. The leadership passed to Captain Yorshka, Gwyndolin's crossbreed sister, who was immediately imprisoned by Sulyvahn. Sulyvahn converted Irithyll's knights to the worship of the Deep. The Pontiff then led his master and Saint of the Deep, Aldrich, to devour the helpless Gwyndolin.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Sulyvahn continued to climb the ranks of the Way of White's clergy and increase his influence until, at one point, Gwyndolin was "stricken by illness" and was forced into retiring from the government of the city, leaving command of the Blades of the Darkmoon to his younger sister Yorshka. The sorcerer took advantage of the situation and proclaimed himself "Pontiff", the legitimate representative of the god, who would act as the ad interim ruler over the realm of Irithyll and as head of the Church. The Silver Knights, still faithful to Gwyndolin, and the Blades of the Darkmoon serving Yorshka could have acted against his wrongful proclamation; therefore Sulyvahn preemptively imprisoned the god in the old cathedral of Anor Londo and his sister on the tower of her church, creating a stalemate in which neither the Silver Knights nor the Blades of the Darkmoon could act, afraid of seeing their captive leaders executed.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: With great foresight and manipulation, Sulyvahn began his rise to power within Irithyll: the sorcerer used the Profaned Flame to enthrall the city's holy knights, corrupting their hearts with the unquenchable version of the Fire they venerated. His influence expanded also to the troops they commanded who became Sulyvahn's personal knights, reporting directly to him, acting as his watchful eyes first and as his designated killers second, effectively becoming his private militia and secret police. Those who were once holy knights became "fire witches" who carried the Profaned Flame of Sulyvahn on Immolation Tinders, also catalysts for the sorcery once so abhorred by the clergy, while the swords of the soldiers they led were imbued with the frost magic of their leader.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : Sulyvahn was a humanoid creature born and raised in the Painted World of Ariandel. Despite his isolation from the outside world, he demonstrated incredible intelligence and talent for sorcery as a young man; he created new frost-based sorceries, using the cold climate of his home to strengthen weapons or form clouds of freezing mist. At some point Sulyvahn became dissatisfied with living inside the Painted World, as he had not experienced the loss or despair of those who ended up there to seek refuge after having lost everything else, and decided to abandon it, leaving behind the sorceries he developed to seek knowledge and experiences in the outside world.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: of the resurrected Lords of Cinder, Aldrich had no intention of sacrificing himself anew, as he had come to believe that an "Age of the Deep" should come and replace the Age of Fire, motivating him to try to devour the gods themselves to erode their hold on the Flame and accelerate the coming of his vision. Gathering an army of deacons from the Cathedral of the Deep, Aldrich, still hungry for flesh and now eager to devour Gods, marched on Irithyll with his followers so that he could devour Gwyndolin, the king of the Gods. He found his way blocked by Sulyvahn and his knights, as the Pontiff had no intention of relinquishing the source of his control over the city and the Way of White without a fight. Aldrich emerged victorious from the ensuing battle, slaughtering Sulyvahn\'s troops and forcing the Pontiff to reluctantly clear the way for the ruined cathedral of Anor Londo. Soul of Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - item - trivia 
 trivia : A more accurate translation of "主神" would be "king god/main deity". This confirms the fact that Gwyndolin, the god who is devoured by Aldrich, had effectively become the leader of the gods of ancient Anor Londo and obtained the place at the helm of the Way of White. To do this he would have to overthrow Allfather Lloyd, Gwyn's uncle who had assumed command while Gwyndolin was still considered a "daughter" of Gwyn.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Sulyvahn consolidated his rule of the church and the city, wielding in his right hand the ceremonial Profaned Greatsword infused with the power of the dark Profaned Flame that had fueled his ambitions and in his left hand the ceremonial Greatsword of Judgment, a symbol of his authority as Gwyndolin's judge, but actually infused with moon magic very close to dark sorcery. The two swords together was not only a representation of the violent rule of Sulyvahn but also an avowal of the Pontiff's dark roots. In fact, the Pontiff spread the practice of sorcery even among the highest ranks of his clergy and his knights and began to carry out various experiments on darkness. The humans who worked on the city were enslaved and reduced to conditions of extreme misery; their Dark Soul would manifest outside their ghostly bodies as monstrous beasts with human faces, wandering the streets. Meanwhile, in the prisons, Sulyvahn tried to transform people into pale dragons, but only managed to produce

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Having gained power in Irithyll, Sulyvahn set about cleansing the city of potential enemies, exiling or killing the Blades of the Darkmoon until there were no more knights in the order, eliminating the Painting Guardians, and even turning the Giants who worked in the city into slaves. The Pontiff would also build an immense dungeon underground near the Profaned Capital, employing its survivors as cruel jailers in his service, and building prisons for humans around the oldest cell of a giant. In addition, Sulyvahn erected a magic barrier around Irithyll to prevent anyone from entering or leaving without his permission, giving special dolls to his most valued subjects to move through it freely, an artifact which reminded them ceaselessly that their "home" would always be the Boreal Valley. title: The Deep
snippet: aldrich_devourer_of_gods_aldrich_saint_of_the_deep : The "peaceful and sacred" Deep would be sharply transformed with the arrival of Aldrich, a Way of White cleric who was practically exiled from his home. Originating from Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, Aldrich was ostensibly a proper man of cloth; however, despite his appearance and status, he was in fact a depraved cleric who took pleasure in devouring humans and indulging in their last screams. Eating people became a routine for Aldrich, keeping it up so long that his own body bloated, becoming melted sludge. With Pontiff Sulyvahn's rise to power in Irithyll, as well as his domination of the Way of White faith within the city, Aldrich's depraved habit became likely to draw unwanted attention to the Pontiff's new "holy" regime. snippet: Despite his coup and the partial schism that saw the Church of Carim establish itself as the alternative political and religious center of the Way of White, Sulyvahn continued to remain an ally of Lothric, donating the Gargoyles he found in the Profaned Capital to the kingdom and allowing their knights and scholars into Irithyll. This powerful alliance allowed the Pontiff to retain international legitimacy and political leverage to strengthen his position and keep other human realms and high members of the clergy faithful to his faction.

 lead : **Pontiff Sulyvahn** ([https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_language Orig.]: 法王サリヴァーン, [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hepburn_romanization Hepburn]: *Hōō Sarivān*) is a mandatory boss in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : Sulyvahn is a tall humanoid clothed in torn ceremonial robes, with nothing on his feet. He wears a crown and is adorned with a necklace of his eye rings. His skin is pale and seems to be decayed and covered in large cracks. His face is covered in dark roots; when he is brought to half of his life, masses of similar roots and branches emerge from his back, akin to wings.

Sulyvahn wields two greatswords: the Profaned Ultra Greatsword in his right hand and the Greatsword of Judgment in his left. When the Ashen One enters the church, Sulyvahn is standing still with his two swords; when approached, his swords start to glow and he advances towards the player before quickly charging with an overhead slash.

During the fight, Sulyvahn can be heard grunting and growling in a deep, distorted voice.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : "Sulyvahn" is phonetically similar to the Irish name "Súileabháin" (related to the more common, Anglicized name "Sullivan") which means "One-eyed" in English. It can also mean "little dark-eyed one" in Irish, which matches the black rings he gives to his knights to devolve them.
**Both names are ironic, given that he lacks eyes.
In Japanese, Sulyvahn's title is written like 法王. This word is used to denote Buddha, and also the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope Pope] - the highest dignitary in Catholic Church. Although the word pontiff technically may be applied to any [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishops_in_the_Catholic_Church bishop], it was implied that Sulyvahn holds the highest possible position in the Church of Irithyll.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - irithyll_and_anor_londo_dark_souls_iii_anor_londo 
 irithyll_and_anor_londo_dark_souls_iii_anor_londo : On the surface, the Ashen One fights their way to the grand church in Irithyll where they find Pontiff Sulyvahn. Killing Sulyvahn opens the way to Anor Londo, fabled city of the gods, where Aldrich awaits. Aldrich, having lost interest in the flame and having instead turned towards the Dark, sought out Anor Londo to devour the gods themselves. He found and devoured Dark Sun Gwyndolin in Anor Londo, who had been "stricken by illness" and had retreated to the Anor Londo Cathedral, only to be imprisoned by the Pontiff to be fed to Aldrich. Fighting their way past the archers protecting the city, the Ashen One finds Aldrich using Gwyndolin as a puppet of sorts, and kills him, acquiring his ashes to be delivered to his throne.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: Sulyvahn would also craft dark eye rings for his Boreal Outrider Knights, an order of knights who were sent away to serve in foreign campaigns as exiles. The Pontiff exploited the Outriders through these rings that would boost their attacks or recover their health as long as their fighting persisted; the process would lead to the Outrider Knights turning into raving, mindless warriors and guards. The end result ensured the unquestioning, unwavering obedience of the ferocious Outrider Knights to the Pontiff. The knights who peered inside the black orbs would be lured into visions of endless deadly battles and go insane, transformed into frenzied beasts. However, the effect of the rings, whose black eyes constantly hound the knights, continues over time, first fusing their armor with their own hide and then devolving them into beasts under the complete control of the Pontiff. At a certain point, Sulyvahn even forced a direct daughter of Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight to serve him as a

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: When Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Emma, the High Priestess of Lothric, would send out messengers bearing the banner of Lothric to ask allied countries for aid in resolving their internal situation. Sulyvahn would respond to his ally's call, ordering his Dancer to serve as a Boreal Outrider Knight in Lothric alongside a division of Boreal Outrider Knights, under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Here she positioned herself to guard the Cathedral and High Priestess Emma while Vordt guarded the main gate of the city and the Outrider Knights infiltrated inside and around the city of Lothric.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their very essence, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder just for his strength, without any consideration for his morality or how he acquired his power. Now left to indulge in his every perversion so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the manor at the outskirts of Irithyll of the Boreal Valley was the house that was granted to Sulyvahn when he was accepted into the society of the nobles. The original description of the bonfire is "Abandoned House on the Outskirts of the City” (街はずれの廃屋)", implying that the Manor was built on the edge of the city as its inhabitant was not equal to the other nobles of divine origins, and that it had become abandoned by the time that Sulyvahn would have ascended to Pontiff. Furthermore, the "Distant Manor" bonfire is en route to the Irithyll Dungeon and consequently the Profaned Capital, where Sulyvahn would find the Profaned Flame below Irithyll, making the access under his house a logical point along his discovery. Curiously, the manor is also the place where the city's sewage system dumped its waste.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: One day, when Sulyvahn was still young, he unearthed the Profaned Capital underneath the outskirts of Irithyll; he also discovered in the ruins of the city the Profaned Flame. It was a "cold" flame, found preserved in icy remains; it was an unfading, everlasting flame, and one that held within it the Dark of humanity. Having obtained the sinful flame, an unquenchable ambition took root in Sulyvahn's heart, as the young man understood its potential as an element of immense political and religious power: The First Flame would eventually fade, while his Profaned Flame was everlasting.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: At one point, Sulyvahn sent McDonnell, an Archdeacon from Irithyll that was a sorcerer despite being a high-ranking cleric, to help the deacons of the Cathedral. McDonnell shared his sorceries with the priests of the Cathedral, who in turn became sorcerers, turning their holy candles into sorcery staves and blades, better equipped to face the abominations of the Deep. However McDonnell would soon find delight in the stagnant souls of the Deep, believing the place to be the "bottom of the world". Over time the deacons themselves, despite their faith and holy flame, began to succumb to the power of the Deep. They began to add dark stories about the Deep to the holy scriptures intended to grant them divine protection, corrupting these holy tales into profanity. McDonnell realized that the rotten darkness of the Deep could become an incredible new power, and by studying it, he created sorceries that manipulated the dark soul dregs, then imparted them to Archdeacon Royce and his deacons.

title: Aldrich Faithful (item)
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful (item) -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Found in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. Obtained by interacting with Archdeacon McDonnell's remains in the Water Reserve and accepting to join the Aldrich Faithful covenant.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed through the level and make way to the opposite side of the big courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Enter the building at the end and hit the wall on the left to reveal a hidden ladder. Climb down and defeat the two Sulyvahn's Beasts lurking at the bottom. Once done, head to the far-left corner of the room to find McDonnell's remains.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - location 
 location : The Aldrich Faithful covenant can be found in the lower plane of Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed onward and make way to the other side of the large courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Upon entering the main building on the opposite side, hit the wall on the left to reveal an illusory wall concealing the main access to the covenant.

Climb down the large ladder to reach a big, flooded hall. There are two Sulyvahn's Beasts lying in wait once reaching this area, one on the left and one further ahead on the right.

In one corner of the room lie the remains of Archdeacon McDonnell. Interacting with him allows access into the covenant.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
In the soul of Aldrich, there is a distinct lighter portion inside the soul that is not present in other deep soul; it is probably what's left of Gwyndolin's soul.
The comic *Dark Souls: The Breath of Andolus* features a scryer named Aldrich as the deuteragonist, potentially as a reference to him, despite them not being the same character. Alternatively, it may have been Aldrich long in the past, given he begins to adopt Aldrich's characteristics, such as cannibalism. While he claims to have been forced into it, the scryer Aldrich is later revealed to be a two faced schemer.
The music played during his fight is a more sinister and macabre arrangement of Gwyndolin's theme from the first game, as he uses the body of the god to defend himself, there are also elements from Nito's theme that are played in the first phase as displayed by the sinister chants and piano notes that are also prevalent in Nito's theme.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich's staff uses a Dark Miracle version of Nito's Gravelord Sword and in the deleted files Aldrich was able to do the Gravelord Sword Dance miracle.
As he is an amalgamation of corpses just like Nito and the Rotten, and his overall resemblance to Nito, it could be theorized that Aldrich is the new gravelord or that he found the soul of the old dead one, which allowed him to pursue his cannibalistic habits further.
In original his name writing like エルドリッチ which can be translated as Eldritch, that means “mystic, unnatural, frightening”, with an association with terror or horror that cannot be comprehended by the human mind. The whole theme of The Deep and Age of Deep Sea may be inspired by such horrors.
In the soul of Aldrich, there is a distinct lighter portion inside the soul that is not present in other deep soul; it is probably what's left of Gwyndolin's soul.

title: Sulyvahn's Beast
snippet:
Sulyvahn's Beast -  Dark Souls III - enemy - description 
 description : Sulyvahn's Beasts are large, ferocious monsters that guard key areas around the city of Irithyll. One of them ambushes the player on the bridge leading into the city, whilst two more guard the Aldrich Faithful covenant. Their abdomen appears to be ripped open, exposing their ribcage.

title: Sulyvahn's Beast
snippet:
Sulyvahn's Beast -  Dark Souls III - enemy - locations 
 locations : Encountered only in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.
One will spawn behind the player as they cross the bridge that leads to Central Irithyll.
Two can be found in the area beyond an illusory wall which leads to the Aldrich Faithful covenant. Defeating them gives access to the Water Reserve bonfire.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet:
There is a statue in the High Wall of Lothric that resembles Sulyvahn, in the square patrolled by the Winged Knight. It depicts a barefooted man in the Robe of Prayer wielding the Profaned Greatsword and wearing bracelets, both of which are on the right wrist, similar to Sulyvahn's own bracelets.
**It is although more likely that the statue is an example of propaganda through symbolism, where the young Prince Lothric, embodiment of the hope of all realms, would carry on the legacy of the Linking of the Fire armed with the Pontiff's Sword, symbol of the support of the Church, strength of Faith and power of the Fire.
The Pontiff seems to lack a face, and the front of his head is instead covered in what looks like roots. Removing his armor and the root-like formations shows a completely featureless face.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Aldrich's throne in Firelink Shrine refers to him as "Saint Aldrich of the Deep".
Before eating Gwyndolin, Aldrich imposed on himself a practice of asceticism (苦行), that is, he refrained from eating humans before he could devour the god.
During the fight, as well as when the boss is passive, shrieks and moans of pain can be heard coming from Gwyndolin. As Aldrich was half-way through consuming Gwyndolin and had used the God's body to defend himself, this disturbingly implies that Gwyndolin was still alive (albeit barely) and in a semi-conscious state of being continuously devoured by Aldrich, even during the fight.
While the attacks of Gwyndolin were light blue energy that dealt magic damage in the first game, Aldrich uses variations of the same attacks with purple energy that dealt dark damage.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
While the attacks of Gwyndolin were light blue energy that dealt magic damage in the first game, Aldrich uses variations of the same attacks with purple energy that dealt dark damage.
Innumerable bones and large amounts of sludge can be seen on the floor of the arena, similar in appearance to Aldrich himself, and possibly being actually part of his body. If this is the case, then, Aldrich insists on attacks by exerting his will over the body of Gwyndolin, instead of simply devouring the player.
The sludge and bones remain after Aldrich dies, though they are inert, making him and Archdeacon Royce the only two bosses to leave behind physical remains.
His melee attacks, during his first phase, closely resemble those of Nito.
Aldrich's staff uses a Dark Miracle version of Nito's Gravelord Sword and in the deleted files Aldrich was able to do the Gravelord Sword Dance miracle.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : Like the Watchdogs of Farron, Aldrich Faithful will be called upon to defend Aldrich's territory from trespassers; any player who has Host of Embers status will be subject to invasion. This area is defined as anywhere from the courtyard upon exiting Pontiff Sulyvahn's arena, up until the rotating stairway leading up to Anor Londo. Aldrich Faithful can pursue trespassers up into the cathedral itself, but will not be summoned for trespassers who have already reached the upper level bonfire.

Defeating the Host of Embers will reward all present Aldrich Faithful with Human Dregs, which can be offered to Archdeacon McDonnell to deepen their allegiance to the covenant.

title: Timeline
snippet:
During the exploration of the Profaned Capital, Sulyvahn discovers the Profaned Flame and its immense power. He takes a greatsword imbued of its power and returns to the capital. With the power to control an everlasting, terrible Flame he's seeing as the carrier of an unprecedented power and begins to rapidly climb the Church's ranks
Once he achieved a key position within the clergy, he de facto takes control of the city and declares himself Pontiff, therefore leader of the Church. Gwyndolin, the worshipped deity, is secluded in the cathedral and Yorshka is promptly imprisoned away from the rest of the world.
The Way of White refuses to officially recognize Sulyvahn new course, therefore a schism erupts within the church, with Irithyll's Pontiff on one side and Carim's Archbishop on the other
The Pontiff allows the clergy to freely study sorcery and creates his own militia to guard the city. The Blades of the Darkmoon are disbanded and removed as a threat to his power

snippet:
The Pontiff allows the clergy to freely study sorcery and creates his own militia to guard the city. The Blades of the Darkmoon are disbanded and removed as a threat to his power
The former aristocrats and maidens of the Profaned Capital surrender to Sulyvahn, accepting to serve as jailers within Irithyll's Dungeon

The Cathedral becomes corrupted by the spreading Deep, therefore Aldrich is chosen as the next Lord of Cinder to link the Fire and cleanse this raging plague

title: Timeline
snippet:
Due to the **Stagnation***, Irithyll* is drawn close to Lothric, submerging the Profaned Capital in the process and near Carthus
The two powers enter in contact. Initial diplomatic exchanges begin
Carim, under pressure from Gwyndolin, assists Lothric to fully embrace the Way of White's doctrine and supports the process of "creating" Fire Keepers to guard more bonfires
Blade of the Darkmoon and Blue Sentinels enter in contact, strengthening the union between Way of White and Way of Blue
Together with the formation of the Undead Settlement, a grand Cathedral is built nearby to provide a place of prayer and indoctrination for the followers
Sulyvahn leaves the Painted World and reaches Irithyll
As a young, talented sorcerer but with limited capabilities, he realizes a rough replica of Gwyndolin's Staff to obtain the favour of the Darkmoon Knights. He's likely given a low position in the Church

title: Way of White
snippet:
The Way of White built a cathedral dedicated to the goddess Caitha and with the aim of cleansing humans from the stagnant darkness within them that was becoming an ever-increasing problem, using the "sacred and peaceful" body of water on which the structure was built to contain all the remnants from its cleansing rituals and even sent three archdeacons to manage it.

At a certain point, the king of the gods Gwyndolin was struck by an "illness" and Sulyvahn took advantage of it, locking the god in the old abandoned cathedral of Anor Londo and proclaiming himself "Pontiff", thus assuming command of the Way of White. This caused a schism within the Way of White, as the Church of Carim and its Archbishop did not recognize Sulyvahn's authority, separating themselves from the denomination of the other Archbishops who kept following the Church of Irithyll.

title: Way of White
snippet: ** Such similarities can also help explaining the dynamic of the schism that emerged within the Way of White after Sulyvahn unilaterally declared himself Pontiff: rejecting his authority, Carim's clergy decided not to recognize Irithyll's position as the legitimate head of the Church, therefore they nominated an Archbishop as the true leader of the Way of White and created a second major sphere of influence in the religious geopolitical scenario. The same thing has taken place in 1054a.D., when the Eastern Roman Empire refused to follow the Pope's lead and created the Orthodox Church, led by the Archbishop of Constantinople.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight
snippet: After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Sulyvahn would order a division of the Outrider Knights to reach Lothric, under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Here they would position themselves in various strategic points of the city, infiltrating the barracks of the Lothric army, the Grand Archives and the Undead Settlement located outside the walls, effectively controlling the places of command and movement of the kingdom.

title: The Deep
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their humanity, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder—just for his strength, without regard for his morality. Now left to indulge in his perversions so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

title: Gods
snippet:
Many Silver Knights since the Age of Ancients served Lord Gwyn and the other Old Gods of Anor Londo, well into the events of *Dark Souls III*. Their origins and species are never clearly explained.
Crossbreed Priscilla, hated by the Gods, was exiled to the Painted World of Ariamis hidden in Anor Londo. She was likely the hybrid daughter of Seath, and the mother of both Gwyndolin, with Gwyn as the father, and of Yorshka, from another father.
Pontiff Sulyvahn, a cleric born in another Painted World and who later came to Anor Londo, where he would forcefully take control of Irithyll from Gwyndolin, becoming its tyrannical ruler.

title: The Deep
snippet: The Deep, as it is encountered in *Dark Souls III*, is likely a corruption of a gentler, more serene "Deep Sea", which was once employed by Way of White clerics in the Cathedral of the Deep for purification purposes. The quietude of the Deep was seemingly disturbed with the arrival of Aldrich, a Way of White cleric hailing from Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. At his home, Aldrich had engaged in grotesque behaviour that presumably alarmed Pontiff Sulyvahn, the leader of the Way of White faith in the city, who decided on posting him at the Cathedral of the Deep— perhaps in hopes that he could benefit from the Cathedral's services to cleanse himself. It seems, however, that the stay of Aldrich was concurrent with the rapid degeneration of the Cathedral and its pond, to which Aldrich presumably contributed greatly.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gods -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Even after the awakening of the Ashen One, the influence of several gods or their descendants is still present in the world.

Dark Sun Gwyndolin, once the king of the gods and of Irithyll, had been imprisoned in the city's old cathedral by Pontiff Sulyvahn, that stripped him of his power to rule in his place. However Aldrich, Devourer of Gods had arrived in Irithyll and, after defeating Sulyvahn, he began to devour Gwyndolin. Yorshka, Gwyndolin'sister, is still alive and leads the knights's of the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant, but she has been imprisoned by Sulyvahn in an isolated tower.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

Once Aldrich defeated Sulyvahn and took control of the city, McDonnell remained to watch over the old Cathedral where the saint was busy digesting Gwyndolin, establishing the covenant of Aldrich Faithful, passing on his dark sorceries to followers who brought him evidence of success in their task.

title: White Preacher Head
snippet:
White Preacher Head -  Dark Souls III - armor - description 
 description : An empty head of a white-faced locust that rose from an abyssal swamp.

The white-faced locusts were meant to beckon men to the dark with sermons, but most of them are unable to think past their own stomachs. Someone must rise to the occasion, and restore the path of righteousness.

Perhaps that someone is you? Did you not arise from the Abyss, and did you not resist drowning in the Age of Fire? Locusts and men are kindred spirits.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell

title: Gods
snippet:
Gods -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : After Lord Gwyn entered the Kiln of the First Flame, most of the gods abandoned Anor Londo, leaving behind a small army of Silver Knights and two elite knights: Dragon Slayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough, to protect the city. Much more shady was the role of Gwyndolin, the only true God that remained in Anor Londo. He created an illusion of Gwynevere, Lord Gwyn's daughter, to hide the fact that she had left Anor Londo and married the Flame God, Flann. Gwyndolin has the same goal as Kingseeker Frampt, using the illusion of Gwynevere to convince the Chosen Undead to rekindle the First Flame. Gwyndolin seems to survive the events of *Dark Souls* as he is being consumed by Aldrich, Devourer of Gods in *Dark Souls III*, implying that the Chosen Undead either did not fight him or only defeated an illusion of him in the timeline canon to the latter game.

title: Lords
snippet:
In his fear of the Age of Dark, he sacrificed himself to the First Flame, prolonging the Age of Fire and becoming Lord of Cinder. This act rendered Gwyn Hollow.

At some point, his firstborn son tamed a stormdrake, and allied with the dragon descendants. For this treachery, he was stripped of his godhood and banished (albeit, not by Gwyn), expunged from all records of history.

title: Classes (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Classes (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Classes** are a gameplay element in *Dark Souls III* and play a major role in Character Creation.

The starting classes available to the player can differ in terms of stats and Soul Level, and serve to determine the player's stats and equipment at the start of the game. However, after the start of the game, the player will be able to level their character into any build, so it could be said that there is no "wrong" starting class to pick.

title: Illusory Wall (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
**From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed onward and make your way to the other side of the large courtyard containing several dead Giant Slaves. Upon entering the main building on the opposite side, hit the wall on the left to reveal a ladder leading downward. Below is a flooded chamber containing two Sulyvahn's Beasts carrying the Ring of Favor, and in the corner of the room can be found the body of Archdeacon McDonnell, used to join the Aldrich Faithful covenant.
**The entrance to Gwyn's honorary tomb, the previous location of the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant and Dark Sun Gwyndolin boss fight in *Dark Souls*, can be found in the same location in Anor Londo. Accessing it is achieved through simply attacking the statue of Gwyn. This illusory wall is already dispelled if the player allowed Anri of Astora to die at the hands of the assassin during Yuria of Londor's questline.

title: Flame God Flann
snippet:
Flame God Flann -  Dark Souls - character - theories 
 theories : As one of the gods with the least amount of information about himself available, despite having the hefty role of marrying Gwynevere, the drive to theorize about his role and place in the world comes naturally. All of the following information is speculation, however, to be taken with a grain of salt.

title: Leydia Pyromancer
snippet: What makes Leydia Pyromancers even deadlier, however, is that they can swarm the player and overwhelm them with massed spells and attacks. Any time one of the bells in their area is rung, a Pyromancer spawns from each of the large tombstones, and can all immediately aggro on the player. In particular, Undead Laborers can rise from the ground and move immediately towards a nearby bell and ring it.
